sanskrit: ṛśyamūkāt sa dharmātmā kiṣkindhāṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ jagāma sahasugrīvo vālivikramapālitām
english: That righteous-souled elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa departed from Ṛśyamūka together with Sugrīva toward Kiṣkindhā, which was guarded by the might of Vāli.

sanskrit: samudyamya mahac cāpaṃ rāmaḥ kāñcanabhūṣitam śarāṃś cāditya saṃkāśān gṛhītvā raṇasādhakān
english: Rāma took up his great bow adorned with gold, and grasped his battle-winning arrows, blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: agratas tu yayau tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ sugrīvaḥ saṃhatagrīvo lakṣmaṇaś ca mahābalaḥ
english: In front of that great-souled Rāghava went Sugrīva with his powerful neck, and mighty Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato hanumān vīro nalo nīlaś ca vānaraḥ tāraś caiva mahātejā hariyūthapa yūthapāḥ
english: Behind came the heroic Hanumān, the monkey Nala, Nīla, and the great-splendored Tāra—leaders of the monkey troops.

sanskrit: te vīkṣamāṇā vṛkṣāṃś ca puṣpabhārāvalambinaḥ prasannāmbuvahāś caiva saritaḥ sāgaraṃ gamāḥ
english: They gazed upon trees bending under the weight of blossoms, and upon rivers bearing clear waters flowing toward the ocean.

sanskrit: kandarāṇi ca śailāṃś ca nirjharāṇi guhās tathā śikharāṇi ca mukhyāni darīś ca priyadarśanāḥ
english: They looked upon caves and mountain ranges, cascading waterfalls, caverns, prominent peaks, and lovely rocky clefts.

sanskrit: vaidūryavimalaiḥ parṇaiḥ padmaiś cākāśakuḍmalaiḥ śobhitān sajalān mārge taṭākāṃś ca vyalokayan
english: Along the way they beheld ponds full of water, beautified by leaves clear as vaidūrya gems and by lotuses with sky-reaching buds.

sanskrit: kāraṇḍaiḥ sārasair haṃsair vañjūlair jalakukkuṭaiḥ cakravākais tathā cānyaiḥ śakunaiḥ pratināditān
english: Those ponds resounded with kāraṇḍava ducks, sārasa cranes, haṃsa geese, vañjūla birds, water-hens, cakravāka pairs, and many other birds.

sanskrit: mṛduśaṣpāṅkurāhārān nirbhayān vanagocarān carataḥ sarvato 'paśyan sthalīṣu hariṇān sthitān
english: On all sides they saw deer standing on open ground, ranging the forest fearlessly, feeding on tender shoots of fresh grass.

sanskrit: taṭākavairiṇaś cāpi śukladantavibhūṣitān ghorān ekacarān vanyān dviradān kūlaghātinaḥ
english: They also saw fearsome wild elephants adorned with white tusks, lone wanderers, enemies of embankments, striding alone through the forest.

sanskrit: vane vanacarāṃś cānyān khecarāṃś ca vihaṃgamān paśyantas tvaritā jagmuḥ sugrīvavaśavartinaḥ
english: Beholding yet other forest-dwelling creatures and sky-roaming birds, those who were subject to Sugrīva's command advanced quickly.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu gacchatāṃ tatra tvaritaṃ raghunandanaḥ drumaṣaṇḍaṃ vanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ sugrīvam abravīt
english: As they hastened along, Rāma the delight of the Raghu lineage, catching sight of a grove of trees, spoke to Sugrīva.

sanskrit: eṣa megha ivākāśe vṛkṣaṣaṇḍaḥ prakāśate meghasaṃghātavipulaḥ paryantakadalīvṛtaḥ
english: "This cluster of trees gleams in the sky like a cloud—vast as a mass of storm-clouds, its borders ringed with plantain trees."

sanskrit: kim etaj jñātum icchāmi sakhe kautūhalaṃ mama kautūhalāpanayanaṃ kartum icchāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: "I wish to know what this is, my friend—I am curious. I want you to relieve my curiosity."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ gacchann evācacakṣe 'tha sugrīvas tan mahad vanam
english: Hearing those words of the great-souled Rāghava, Sugrīva, even as he walked on, described that great forest.

sanskrit: etad rāghava vistīrṇam āśramaṃ śramanāśanam udyānavanasaṃpannaṃ svādumūlaphalodakam
english: "O Rāghava, this is a vast hermitage, a destroyer of fatigue, endowed with gardens and woodland, rich in sweet roots, fruits, and water."

sanskrit: atra saptajanā nāma munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ saptaivāsann adhaḥśīrṣā niyataṃ jalaśāyinaḥ
english: "Here dwell sages known as the Seven Persons, of sharpened vows—seven in number, who remain with heads downward, ever lying in the water."

sanskrit: saptarātrakṛtāhārān vāyunā vanavāsinaḥ divaṃ varṣaśatair yātāḥ saptabhiḥ sakalevarāḥ
english: "They eat once every seven nights, they subsist on air, dwelling in the forest; over seven centuries they have ascended to heaven, still embodied."

sanskrit: teṣām evaṃ prabhāvena drumaprākārasaṃvṛtam āśramaṃ sudurādharṣam api sendraiḥ surāsuraiḥ
english: "By their power this hermitage, encircled by a wall of trees, has become utterly unconquerable—even by gods and demons together with Indra."

sanskrit: pakṣiṇo varjayanty etat tathānye vanacāriṇaḥ viśanti mohād ye 'py atra nivartante na te punaḥ
english: "Birds avoid this place, as do other forest-wanderers; those who enter it through delusion do not return."

sanskrit: vibhūṣaṇaravāś cātra śrūyante sakalākṣarāḥ tūryagītasvanāś cāpi gandho divyaś ca rāghava
english: "From here, O Rāghava, are heard the distinct sounds of ornaments, and strains of music and song, and a divine fragrance."

sanskrit: tretāgnayo 'pi dīpyante dhūmo hy eṣa pradṛśyate veṣṭayann iva vṛkṣāgrān kapotāṅgāruṇo ghanaḥ
english: "The three sacred fires still blaze here; that smoke is visible, a dense pigeon-gray-red column, wrapping itself around the treetops."

sanskrit: kuru praṇāmaṃ dharmātmaṃs tān samuddiśya rāghavaḥ lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā prayataḥ saṃyatāñjaliḥ
english: "O righteous-souled Rāghava, offer obeisance to them—reverently, with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, with palms joined."

sanskrit: praṇamanti hi ye teṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām na teṣām aśubhaṃ kiṃ cic charīre rāma dṛśyate
english: "For those who bow to these enlightened sages, O Rāma, no misfortune whatsoever is seen to afflict their bodies."

sanskrit: tato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena kṛtāñjaliḥ samuddiśya mahātmānas tān ṛṣīn abhyavādayat
english: Thereupon Rāma, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, with palms joined, directed his obeisance toward those great-souled sages and reverently saluted them.

sanskrit: abhivādya ca dharmātmā rāmo bhrātā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ sugrīvo vānarāś caiva jagmuḥ saṃhṛṣṭamānasāḥ
english: Having paid their salutations, the righteous-souled Rāma, his brother Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva, and the monkeys proceeded with joyful hearts.

sanskrit: te gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ tasmāt saptajanāśramāt dadṛśus tāṃ durādharṣāṃ kiṣkindhāṃ vālipālitām
english: Having traveled a great distance from that hermitage of the Seven Persons, they beheld Kiṣkindhā, that impregnable city, ruled by Vāli.

sanskrit: sarve te tvaritaṃ gatvā kiṣkindhāṃ vālipālitām vṛkṣair ātmānam āvṛtya vyatiṣṭhan gahane vane
english: All of them, having swiftly reached Kiṣkindhā ruled by Vāli, concealed themselves among trees and stood in the dense forest.

sanskrit: vicārya sarvato dṛṣṭiṃ kānane kānanapriyaḥ sugrīvo vipulagrīvaḥ krodham āhārayad bhṛśam
english: Casting his glance all around the forest, Sugrīva who delighted in the forest—broad-necked—roused his anger fiercely.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa ninadaṃ ghoraṃ kṛtvā yuddhāya cāhvayat parivāraiḥ parivṛto nādair bhindann ivāmbaram
english: Then, surrounded by his retinue, he let out a terrible roar, as if splitting the sky with his cries, challenging Vāli to battle.

sanskrit: atha bālārkasadṛśo dṛptasiṃhagatis tadā dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ kriyādakṣaṃ sugrīvo vākyam abravīt
english: Then Sugrīva, radiant as the morning sun, with the gait of a proud lion, seeing Rāma skilled in action, spoke these words.

sanskrit: harivāgurayā vyāptaṃ taptakāñcanatoraṇām prāptāḥ sma dhvajayantrāḍhyāṃ kiṣkindhāṃ vālinaḥ purīm
english: "We have arrived at the city of Kiṣkindhā belonging to Vāli—filled with monkey nets, with portals of burnished gold, abundant with flagstaffs and devices."

sanskrit: pratijñā yā tvayā vīra kṛtā vālivadhe purā saphalāṃ tāṃ kuru kṣipraṃ latāṃ kāla ivāgataḥ
english: "The pledge you made earlier, O hero, regarding the slaying of Vāli—now fulfill it swiftly, like the season of fruiting come for the vine."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dharmātmā sugrīveṇa sa rāghavaḥ tam athovāca sugrīvaṃ vacanaṃ śatrusūdanaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Sugrīva, that righteous-souled Rāghava, destroyer of enemies, then spoke these words to Sugrīva.

sanskrit: kṛtābhijñāna cihnas tvam anayā gajasāhvayā viparīta ivākāśe sūryo nakṣatra mālayā
english: "You must bear a distinguishing mark, by means of this garland of gaja flowers, so that I may know you—as the sun in the sky is distinct from the garland of stars."

sanskrit: adya vālisamutthaṃ te bhayaṃ vairaṃ ca vānara ekenāhaṃ pramokṣyāmi bāṇamokṣeṇa saṃyuge
english: "Today, O monkey, I shall free you in a single stroke—releasing one arrow in battle—from both the fear and the enmity arising from Vāli."

sanskrit: mama darśaya sugrīvavairiṇaṃ bhrātṛrūpiṇam vālī vinihato yāvad vane pāṃsuṣu veṣṭate
english: "Show me Vāli, the enemy of Sugrīva who wears the form of a brother—so that he may writhe in the forest dust when struck down."

sanskrit: yadi dṛṣṭipathaṃ prāpto jīvan sa vinivartate tato doṣeṇa mā gacchet sadyo garhec ca mā bhavān
english: "If he comes within range of my sight and yet retreats alive, then let that fault not fall on me—and you must not blame me then."

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ sapta te sālā mayā bāṇena dāritāḥ tato vetsi balenādya bālinaṃ nihataṃ mayā
english: "Before your eyes I pierced seven śāla trees with a single arrow—know by that power that Vāli is today already slain by me."

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me vīra kṛcchre 'pi tiṣṭhatā dharmalobhaparītena na ca vakṣye kathaṃ cana
english: "I have never spoken an untruth, O hero, even in the most difficult circumstances, overwhelmed though I may be by desire for righteousness—nor shall I ever speak one."

sanskrit: saphalāṃ ca kariṣyāmi pratijñāṃ jahi saṃbhramam prasūtaṃ kalamaṃ kṣetre varṣeṇeva śatakratuḥ
english: "I shall fulfill my pledge—abandon your agitation. As Indra of a hundred sacrifices brings rain to make the sown grain sprout in the field, so shall it be."

sanskrit: tadāhvānanimittaṃ tvaṃ vālino hemamālinaḥ sugrīva kuru taṃ śabdaṃ niṣpated yena vānaraḥ
english: "Therefore, for the purpose of that challenge, O Sugrīva, make that sound which will cause the golden-garlanded Vāli, that monkey, to rush forth."

sanskrit: jitakāśī jayaślāghī tvayā cādharṣitaḥ purāt niṣpatiṣyaty asaṃgena vālī sa priyasaṃyugaḥ
english: "That Vāli who glories in victory, who boasts of conquest, who loves combat—having been challenged and provoked by you, he will spring forth from the city without hesitation."

sanskrit: ripūṇāṃ dharṣaṇaṃ śūrā marṣayanti na saṃyuge jānantas tu svakaṃ vīryaṃ strīsamakṣaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: "Heroes do not endure provocation by enemies in battle, especially when they know their own valor—and all the more so before the eyes of women."

sanskrit: sa tu rāmavacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo hemapiṅgalaḥ nanarda krūranādena vinirbhindann ivāmbaram
english: Then Sugrīva, tawny as gold, hearing Rāma's words, roared with a fierce and terrible cry, as if cleaving the sky asunder.

sanskrit: tasya śabdena vitrastā gāvo yānti hataprabhāḥ rājadoṣaparāmṛṣṭāḥ kulastriya ivākulāḥ
english: Terrified by his sound, cows scattered, their brightness dimmed, distraught like noblewomen afflicted by the vice of a king.

sanskrit: dravanti ca mṛgāḥ śīghraṃ bhagnā iva raṇe hayāḥ patanti ca khagā bhūmau kṣīṇapuṇyā iva grahāḥ
english: Deer fled swiftly, like horses broken and routed in battle; birds fell to the ground, like planets whose merit is exhausted.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa jīmūtagaṇapraṇādo nādaṃ vyamuñcat tvarayā pratītaḥ sūryātmajaḥ śauryavivṛddhatejāḥ saritpatir vānilacañcalormiḥ
english: Then that son of the Sun, with valor-enhanced splendor, confident and swift, sent forth a roar like the thunder of gathered storm-clouds—like the lord of rivers whose waves are stirred by the wind.

sanskrit: atha tasya ninādaṃ taṃ sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ śuśrāvāntaḥpuragato vālī bhrātur amarṣaṇaḥ
english: Then Vāli, intolerant of his brother, who was within the inner apartments, heard that roar of the great-souled Sugrīva.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu tasya ninadaṃ sarvabhūtaprakampanam madaś caikapade naṣṭaḥ krodhaś cāpatito mahān
english: Hearing that roar which made all creatures tremble, in an instant his intoxication vanished and great fury descended upon him.

sanskrit: sa tu roṣaparītāṅgo vālī saṃdhyātapaprabhaḥ uparakta ivādityaḥ sadyo niṣprabhatāṃ gataḥ
english: Vāli, his body suffused with rage, blazed like the reddened sun at twilight—and instantly became as it were stripped of his calm radiance.

sanskrit: vālī daṃṣṭrā karālas tu krodhād dīptāgnisaṃnibhaḥ bhāty utpatitapadmābhaḥ samṛṇāla iva hradaḥ
english: Vāli with his fearsome fangs, resembling blazing fire in his wrath, shone like a pond whose lotuses have sprung up together with their stalks.

sanskrit: śabdaṃ durmarṣaṇaṃ śrutvā niṣpapāta tato hariḥ vegena caraṇanyāsair dārayann iva medinīm
english: Hearing that unbearable sound, the monkey lord sprang forth with such speed that the stamp of his feet seemed to split the earth.

sanskrit: taṃ tu tārā pariṣvajya snehād darśitasauhṛdā uvāca trastasaṃbhrāntā hitodarkam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: But Tārā, embracing him and showing her affection from love, frightened and agitated, spoke to him these words bearing beneficial consequences.

sanskrit: sādhu krodham imaṃ vīra nadī vegam ivāgatam śayanād utthitaḥ kālyaṃ tyaja bhuktām iva srajam
english: "It is well, O hero—restrain this anger that has swept in like a river in spate; having just risen from your bed at daybreak, put it away like a garland already enjoyed."

sanskrit: sahasā tava niṣkrāmo mama tāvan na rocate śrūyatām abhidhāsyāmi yannimittaṃ nivāryase
english: "Your sudden sally does not please me. Hear me—I shall tell you the reason why you are being restrained."

sanskrit: pūrvam āpatitaḥ krodhāt sa tvām āhvayate yudhi niṣpatya ca nirastas te hanyamāno diśo gataḥ
english: "Before, he came upon you in anger and challenged you to combat; but when he was repulsed by you and lay nearly slain, he fled in all directions."

sanskrit: tvayā tasya nirastasya pīḍitasya viśeṣataḥ ihaitya punar āhvānaṃ śaṅkāṃ janayatīva me
english: "That he returns here now to challenge you again, after having been so utterly routed and afflicted by you—this arouses my suspicion."

sanskrit: darpaś ca vyavasāyaś ca yādṛśas tasya nardataḥ ninādasya ca saṃrambho naitad alpaṃ hi kāraṇam
english: "The pride and resolve that can be read in his roaring, and the fierce urgency of that cry—this is no small cause for concern."

sanskrit: nāsahāyam ahaṃ manye sugrīvaṃ tam ihāgatam avaṣṭabdhasahāyaś ca yam āśrityaiṣa garjati
english: "I do not think Sugrīva has come here without allies; he roars here relying on some powerful support."

sanskrit: prakṛtyā nipuṇaś caiva buddhimāṃś caiva vānaraḥ aparīkṣitavīryeṇa sugrīvaḥ saha naiṣyati
english: "That monkey is by nature shrewd and wise; Sugrīva would not go to combat alongside one whose valor he has not tested."

sanskrit: pūrvam eva mayā vīra śrutaṃ kathayato vacaḥ aṅgadasya kumārasya vakṣyāmi tvā hitaṃ vacaḥ
english: "Even before now, O hero, I heard words from Prince Aṅgada's account; I shall now speak to you words that are for your good."

sanskrit: tava bhrātur hi vikhyātaḥ sahāyo raṇakarkaśaḥ rāmaḥ parabalāmardī yugāntāgnir ivotthitaḥ
english: "Your brother's ally is the renowned and battle-hardened Rāma, crusher of enemy armies, arisen like the fire of the world's end."

sanskrit: nivāsavṛkṣaḥ sādhūnām āpannānāṃ parā gatiḥ ārtānāṃ saṃśrayaś caiva yaśasaś caikabhājanam
english: "He is the sheltering tree of the virtuous, the ultimate refuge of those who are distressed, the support of the afflicted, and the sole vessel of glory."

sanskrit: jñānavijñānasaṃpanno nideśo nirataḥ pituḥ dhātūnām iva śailendro guṇānām ākaro mahān
english: "Endowed with knowledge and realized wisdom, devoted to his father's command—like the king of mountains is to minerals, he is a great mine of virtues."

sanskrit: tatkṣamaṃ na virodhas te saha tena mahātmanā durjayenāprameyena rāmeṇa raṇakarmasu
english: "Therefore it is not fitting that you enter into conflict with that great-souled Rāma, who is unconquerable and immeasurable in the deeds of battle."

sanskrit: śūra vakṣyāmi te kiṃ cin na cecchāmy abhyasūyitum śrūyatāṃ kriyatāṃ caiva tava vakṣyāmi yad dhitam
english: "O hero, I will tell you something—I do not wish to be censured for it. Listen, and do as I counsel; I shall tell you what is for your welfare."

sanskrit: yauvarājyena sugrīvaṃ tūrṇaṃ sādhv abhiṣecaya vigrahaṃ mā kṛthā vīra bhrātrā rājan balīyasā
english: "Quickly and properly install Sugrīva as crown prince; do not, O hero and king, enter into conflict with a brother who is backed by a mightier power."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi te kṣamaṃ manye tava rāmeṇa sauhṛdam sugrīveṇa ca saṃprītiṃ vairam utsṛjya dūrataḥ
english: "I truly believe what befits you is friendship with Rāma and reconciliation with Sugrīva—casting enmity far away."

sanskrit: lālanīyo hi te bhrātā yavīyān eṣa vānaraḥ tatra vā sann ihastho vā sarvathā bandhur eva te
english: "This younger monkey is your brother who deserves to be cherished; whether he is there or here, he is in every way still your kinsman."

sanskrit: yadi te matpriyaṃ kāryaṃ yadi cāvaiṣi māṃ hitām yācyamānaḥ prayatnena sādhu vākyaṃ kuruṣva me
english: "If my good is dear to you, and if you consider me well-wishing, then, earnestly entreated, heed my words well."
